title: Drop the 2p rise in tax on rental income
name: Drop the 2p rise in tax on rental income
noun: dropping the rise in tax on rental income
headline: Drop the rent income rise. Costs £0.4bn in 2029-30.
description: From April 2027 landlords pay two percentage points more income tax on their property income at every rate. Switch this on to drop the rise.

baselinePolicy.text: Income tax on property income is two percentage points higher at the basic, higher and additional rates from 6 April 2027 (Table 6.1 line 61).

source.quote: This measure increases tax on property income for unincorporated landlords by adding 2 percentage points across the basic rate, higher rate and additional rate.

alreadyIncludes: Income tax on property income is two percentage points higher at the basic, higher and additional rates from 6 April 2027 (Table 6.1 line 61).

lines.title: Property Income: Increase tax rates on property income by 2ppts at the basic, higher and additional rate from 6 April 2027

rawSource.note: Reversal: the Treasury’s costing with its sign reversed (positive scorecard values reduce borrowing; here receipts positive means more revenue).

caveats: The Treasury’s costing is on the OBR October 2026 forecast, the baseline used here. Effects before the start year are not applied: 2026-27 falls before any Budget of yours.
The OBR rates this costing as highly uncertain: landlords can incorporate to avoid it (October 2026 outlook, Table 3.3).

considerations.text: The Treasury’s scorecard figure is the certified direct costing for the measure, including the behavioural response the Treasury and OBR agreed; the Budget 2026 policy costings document gives the method.

interactions.text: Both change the rates on property income: Budget 2025’s two points and this Budget’s two more.
